scan-bot: [FINDING] SAST (repo infra/terraform) detected HIGH-severity: potential KMS key id embedded in template variable -> evidence: path modules/ci/keys.tf line 12. Marking as sensitive. @eng-security please advise

rachel: thanks. can someone paste the finding details? I see references to projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/artifacts in the diff.

morgan: yep that's from PR #3287 (infra/ci-keys). The terraform variable was templated from a legacy env var. Not an actual secret, but points at a stable key name which we treat as sensitive.

pavel: two concerns: 1) scanner flagged it as secret which triggers auto-block, 2) owning team unclear — infra or infra-secrets? We also changed RBAC for keystore roles last week.

ilana: owning team is infra-secrets. PR author pinged them but no approval yet. For RBAC: we removed group 'ci-admins' from keystore binding last Friday.

rachel: can we validate whether this exposure actually grants access to the key? run a quick audit log query for any decrypt attempts from PR author CI.

pavel: query I used: `gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"serviceAccount:pr-author@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" AND protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\"" --limit 5` returned no recent decrypts.

morgan: CI job attempted no decrypt during PR validation; the reference only contains the key resource name. Still we treat it as sensitive naming info per policy.

ilana: operational decision: exclude this finding with an evidence note if infra-secrets confirms no secret materialization and PR adds no permission changes. We need an approval path in the scanner UX instead of immediate auto-block.

sec-oncall: agree. short-term: move to 'needs-review' not 'blocked' for infra repo. Long-term: 1) scanner rule tuning to differentiate resource names vs private keys, 2) a premerge policy that requires owning-team signoff for KMS naming exposures, 3) annotated audit logs with PR id.

rachel: filing SEC-2045 to track runbook + scanner UX: will include exact `gcloud` queries, example evidence template, and an exemption workflow (time-limited). https://issues.redwood.ai/SEC-2045

pavel: also propose adding a bot shortcut in GH checks to 'request owning-team review' which auto-creates an issue and pings infra-secrets with evidence.

morgan: let's also add a safe-list of allowed key-name patterns for public infra repos to reduce noise (but controlled by infra-secrets approvers).

ilana: noted. I'll review and add gate for RBAC changes: PRs touching iam bindings that affect `roles/cloudkms.*` should require an explicit owning-team approval label.

sec-oncall: closure steps: temporary scanner rule change, runbook update, GH check button + issue template, add audit correlation id to CI. I'll own SEC-2045 until all PRs merged.

rachel: thanks all. small ask: add the audit log query and the terraform diff snippet to the runbook so responders can triage faster. :+1:

morgan: will attach diffs to SEC-2045. closing thread once runbook PR merged.
